Amelia —

Appreciate the clarity. I put together a short MAP-style plan (attached: finlytics_map_v1.xlsx) and a simple benchmarking playbook below. High-level timeline:
- Week 1 (Mar 22–26): onboarding, test corpus validation, infra provisioning (hosted + dedicated pilot)
- Week 2 (Mar 29–Apr 2): throughput runs (tokens/sec sustained), peak QPS ramp, and unit-cost model generation
- Apr 3–4: run regression suite and produce final MAP summary for procurement/PO

Benchmarks we will capture (definitions):
- Sustained QPS: mean QPS measured over a 10-minute window under steady-state load (target windows at 5m, 10m, 30m)
- Tokens/sec: encoder+decode tokens processed/sec per GPU normalized to request mix
- Latency/TTFT: time-to-first-token and p50/p95/p99 latencies for both 1k and 10k concurrent virtual users
- Concurrency profile: steady (long tail of small requests) + bursty (50% of traffic in 30s spikes)

Acceptance criteria proposal (examples):
- p95 TTFT <= 350ms for interactive endpoint at 1k concur; <= 550ms at 10k concur (with autoscaling rules)
- Sustained QPS >= 120 req/s for their top endpoint under dedicated pool with x2 replication
- Tokens/sec >= 48k tokens/sec on our 8xA100 pilot (normalized)
- Unit cost: under $X per 1M generated tokens (we'll produce variants for hosted vs. dedicated).

I'll coordinate the runs — Rishi will own the infra scripts, Ben will own cost modeling and the cost snapshot PDF.

Next steps: can you confirm preferred test window(s) next week and whether the traffic will come from a single region? Also confirm whether Finlytics will allow short-lived synthetic keys for the dedicated testing.

Thanks,
Priyom
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
